approval_rules.description: Restricted datasets also need approval from a security analyst. Translated from ServiceNow business rule 7484ac5069d1c0419700a00e33166a37.
Every data access request needs approval from the dataset's owner. Translated from ServiceNow business rule 873937971757a9ca284b1898da024ae1.
During the financial year-end close (22 to 31 March), finance data also needs approval from a finance controller. Translated from ServiceNow business rule e3aeefc1904406b20dadf3bc8e068853.

source_rules.note: Not an approval rule. It rejects data access requests unless u_cost_centre matches CC-1234. ContosoAccessRequest.cost_centre already expresses this: it is declared from u_cost_centre and has the pattern ^CC-[0-9]{4}$. Schema validation enforces it, so the script can be retired. One difference to note: the script makes the field mandatory, but the slot is not marked required in the model. To keep that behaviour, mark cost_centre as required on ContosoAccessRequest.

The script's hard-coded list (client_master, counterparty_exposure, gl_actuals, payroll) is exactly the set of restricted datasets, so it becomes min_classification: restricted. That way a dataset reclassified to restricted is covered automatically. The script names one person, sys_id 5bb1f05607167c49e249269b9e713986 (una.mensah, the 'security team lead'). Policy is written over roles, so this becomes approver_role security-analyst. As a result, una.mensah, amaya.kim and fay.doyle can all approve, not just una.mensah. If only the lead should approve, that needs a narrower role.

The script builds an approver from two hand-maintained maps: dataset to domain, then domain to owner sys_id. Both maps agree with the record today: each dataset's domain and owner match its domain and owner fields. All 12 datasets are mapped, so there is no domain or classification limit. This becomes approver_kind dataset_owner, which reads the owner from the record. The 'updated by hand when owners change' drift risk goes away.

The script's list (budget_forecast, gl_actuals) is exactly the finance domain, so it becomes domain: finance. The window is 22 to 31 March inclusive, which is 10 days, so year_end_close_days: 10. The script compares dates in UTC. The hard-coded approver ba7c24798865d7a0e8f81525b07211d3 (una.tanaka) becomes approver_role finance-controller, so olu.lindqvist, max.kim, zane.doyle and una.tanaka can approve. This rule acts only once a year, so its usage data looks dead. Keep it, don't retire it.
